notes: Lockheed Martin acquired the helicopter maker from United Technologies for $9B, adding the Black Hawk and CH-53K programs to its rotary-wing portfolio.
Leidos absorbed Lockheed Martin's IT and technical services division via a Reverse Morris Trust, creating the largest US federal IT provider at the time.
General Dynamics acquired the Woods Hole Oceanographic spinoff and developer of autonomous underwater vehicles widely deployed by the US Navy for mine countermeasures and ISR.
Northrop paid $7.8B cash plus assumed $1.4B debt for the rocket motors and ammunition manufacturer, folding it in as the new Innovation Systems sector.
Safran completed a tender offer and then absorbed the French aircraft cabin and systems maker via a shareholder merger vote in late 2018.
Thales acquired the digital identity and security giant to create a global leader in cybersecurity, SIM-based credentials, and encryption for defense and government clients.
Elbit acquired the Israeli state-owned arms maker — manufacturer of the Uzi, Galil, and large-calibre munitions — in the largest-ever Israeli defense industry consolidation.
General Dynamics paid $40.75 per share for the federal IT services firm, creating a combined ~$9.9B revenue government technology services unit.
The all-stock merger of equals created L3Harris Technologies with a $34B market cap — the largest-ever pure-play defense sector merger — closing in June 2019.
TransDigm acquired the aerospace and defense components maker with ~$2B in annual revenue, adding cockpit display systems, avionics interfaces, and sensors.
SAIC's all-stock acquisition of the defense analytics and IT services firm created the second-largest US government technology integrator with $6.5B in combined revenue.
Textron Systems acquired the Maine-based developer of the Ripsaw tracked robotic ground vehicle to fill its autonomous land-systems gap across air, land, and sea domains.
The all-stock merger of equals formed Raytheon Technologies (later RTX), combining Collins Aerospace and Pratt & Whitney with Raytheon's missiles and defense businesses.
L3Harris acquired Viasat's Link-16 tactical data link product line and related airborne radio portfolio, consolidating its dominance in NATO-standard battlefield communications.
Leidos acquired the Huntsville-based advanced systems developer to deepen its hypersonics, space, directed-energy, and autonomy work for DoD customers.
TransDigm acquired Cobham's aerospace antenna and radio business — a proprietary connectivity components provider used on major defense platforms — with ~$225M in annual revenue.
Parsons acquired the space, cyber, and intelligence firm — with 50+ Space Force ground control products — for $300M to expand its national security and space portfolio.
Lockheed's proposed acquisition of the sole independent US rocket-motor supplier was terminated in February 2022 after the FTC sued to block the deal on antitrust grounds.
Leonardo acquired a 25.1% strategic stake in the German defense electronics company spun off from Airbus, forging a pan-European sensing and electronic warfare partnership.
AeroVironment acquired the German UGV maker (telemax, tEODor EVO EOD robots) to extend its unmanned systems portfolio from air into ground domains.
Voyager Space took a majority stake in the ISS payload and airlock operator; the combined entity later won a $160M NASA contract with Lockheed Martin to build the Starlab commercial space station.
Veritas Capital and Elliott's Evergreen Coast took the defense C4ISR, training, and transit ticketing technology company private at $75 per share.
Teledyne acquired the world's leading infrared sensor and camera maker for $8B in cash and stock, combining FLIR's defense-sensing portfolio with Teledyne's digital imaging instrumentation.
Shield AI acquired the DARPA AlphaDogfight Trial winner — whose AI beat a human F-16 pilot 5-0 in simulation — to accelerate its autonomous AI pilot program.

Parker Hannifin acquired the UK aerospace and defense components maker at 800p per share, completing the deal in September 2022 after UK government clearance with aircraft wheel/brake divestiture conditions.
US PE-backed Cobham acquired the UK defense electronics company at 3,500p per share; the deal required a 15-month national security review and binding undertakings from the UK government.
Boeing invested an additional $450M in its autonomous eVTOL air-taxi JV with Kitty Hawk (Larry Page), positioning Wisk as one of the best-funded autonomous aviation startups.
BAE Systems acquired the defense simulation and synthetic training environment software maker to expand its digital warfare and virtual mission rehearsal capabilities.
Textron acquired the Slovenian electric aircraft pioneer — manufacturer of the world's first EASA-certified electric plane — seeding its new Textron eAviation segment.
Anduril acquired the autonomous underwater vehicle startup to extend its multi-domain autonomous systems portfolio into maritime and undersea ISR and strike missions.
L3Harris acquired the rocket propulsion and energetics maker at $58 per share in an all-cash deal, completing in July 2023 after the FTC declined to block it.
Carlyle Group took the defense IT and cyber services contractor private at $96 per share to accelerate growth in intelligence analytics and digital transformation for US government clients.
Booz Allen Hamilton acquired the intelligence community-focused classified software and analytics firm to accelerate its TechSIGINT, AI/ML, and cyber mission capabilities.
US-listed Leonardo DRS merged with the Israeli active electronically scanned array radar startup, creating a combined Nasdaq-traded defense electronics company (ticker: DRS).
BAE Systems acquired Ball Corporation's aerospace division — covering space sensors, spacecraft, and electronic warfare systems — to strengthen its US defense electronics footprint.
Rheinmetall acquired the Spanish ammunition producer to rapidly expand artillery shell, mortar, and rocket propellant output amid surging post-Ukraine conflict demand.
Anduril acquired the North Carolina-based developer of the Fury Group 5 jet-powered autonomous combat drone to expand its collaborative combat aircraft program.
Anduril acquired the solid rocket propellant startup to vertically integrate propulsion for its growing family of autonomous missiles and loitering munitions.

target: Rheinmetall Ukrainian Defense Industry LLC (JV with Ukroboronprom)
notes: Rheinmetall formed a joint venture with Ukraine's state defense conglomerate to co-produce armored vehicles, artillery, and ammunition inside Ukraine amid the ongoing conflict.
Boeing announced a reacquisition of its former fuselage supplier at $37.25 per share (all-stock) to restore quality control following the 737 MAX door-plug safety crisis.

Lockheed Martin acquired the small satellite manufacturer — a Lockheed strategic partner since 2017 — completing the deal in October 2024 to vertically integrate low-cost defense satellite production.
Axon (maker of Tasers and body cameras) acquired the German-founded counter-drone detection and C-UAS platform to expand into air security for military, law enforcement, and critical infrastructure.
Palantir was awarded a $178M US Army contract to deliver 10 TITAN AI-driven mobile ground intelligence systems integrating space sensor data for real-time targeting.
Rheinmetall and Hungary's government established a JV to produce Lynx KF41 infantry fighting vehicles at a Zalaegerszeg factory; first Hungarian-made vehicle rolled out in January 2023.
Kratos acquired the microwave amplifier and component maker to vertically integrate EW and satcom hardware capabilities within its growing unmanned and EW systems business.
Kratos acquired the communication product firm to expand its satellite and tactical radio product lines in support of US Space Force and Army programs.
RTX acquired the Boulder-based smallsat bus and spacecraft manufacturer to add high-precision low-cost satellite production for defense and intelligence constellation programs.
Hensoldt signed a €10M agreement to integrate its MSSR 2000 ID Identification-Friend-or-Foe technology into IAI subsidiary ELTA's next-generation air-defense radar systems.
Shield AI acquired the Australian AI-based wide-area motion imagery and automatic target recognition software company to enhance its autonomous ISR capabilities for military aircraft.
Anduril acquired the commercial space domain awareness company providing ground-based telescope networks for tracking satellites and space debris, expanding into the space defense domain.
